title: Give My Regards to Black Jack
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Eijiro Saito, an idealistic intern at the prestigious Eiroku University hospital, is paid so little that he moonlights at an understaffed emergency room. Across the two hospitals he confronts a medical system of long hours, bullying, profit-driven billing and indifferent or corrupt doctors, and asks what being a doctor really means (Manga Club blurb via AniList; MangaUpdates; Manga Bookshelf review).
life_message: A doctor's first duty is to the patient, even when the system rewards profit and silence.

content.note: Accident victims and surgery; little interpersonal violence noted.
Manga Bookshelf: 'mangled flesh and pulsating organs'; MangaUpdates: death.
Nudity in medical context (MangaUpdates; AniList); romantic subplot.
Suicide and tragedy as AniList spoiler tags; single source (to verify).

dominant: Medical-system critique; patient-first humanism; professional virtue

frames.aligns: Dignity of every patient and care for the poor.
frames.concerns: Surgical gore; suicide theme to verify.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Duty to all patients equally, rich or poor.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Critiques rigid hospital hierarchy and seniority.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Medical science and reason drive the story.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Overwork and low pay versus finding meaning in work.

folkways.japan: Strict seniority in Japanese university hospitals (the ikyoku system), unpaid overwork and reluctance to challenge superiors are the targets of the series' critique.

delivery.evidence: Manga Bookshelf calls it effective 'agit-prop' and a 'hectoring medical procedural' whose idealism takes 'simplistic stands on complex issues'.

personified.character: Hospital doctors who take bribes or belittle poor patients

delivery.note: The series argues openly against Japan's hospital system; one reviewer finds its drama too tidy, though some senior doctors are shown with reasons of their own.

winners_losers: Sympathy rests with Saito and patients failed by the system; profit-minded doctors and hospital hierarchy are the targets.
to_verify: Only one review (volumes 1-2) consulted; later arcs (AniList spoiler tags: suicide, tragedy) not confirmed by a second source, so mental-health score capped.
Whether some establishment doctors receive a fairer hearing in later volumes.
English availability: the author made the work freely usable in 2012 (MangaUpdates), with several digital English releases.
